chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who caught a bird in the unrestricted area (al-Hill), bought it, and brought it into the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and it died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If, when he brought it into the Sanctuary, he released its way (let it go free) and it died, then there is nothing upon him; and if he kept it until it died with him inside the Sanctuary, then upon him is the expiation (fidyah).'

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically the sacred area of Mecca where hunting is prohibited)
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The unrestricted area outside the sacred boundaries of Mecca
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: The expiation or compensation due for violating the sanctity of the Haram
key_terms.خَلَّى سَبِيلَهُ: He released its way (let it go free)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a bird caught in the Haram that dies while kept captive?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the liability of fidyah in hunting within the Haram boundaries by distinguishing between natural death after release and death while in captivity, a nuance emphasized by Shia jurists to determine the exact moment of obligation. It reflects the practical application of Quranic injunctions, where the act of 'keeping' or 'detaining' the game triggers the penalty, aligning with the scholarly interpretation of 'holding' in the relevant verse. This distinction highlights the precision of Imami fiqh in differentiating between passive and active possession during the state of Ihram.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibn Bukeyr who said,

‘I asked one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about a man who came across a bird in the unrestricted area. She bought it and entered with it into the Al-Harram, and it died. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that when he entered it into the Al-Harram, freed its way, so it died, then there is nothing upon him; and if it was such that he withheld it until it died with him inside the Al-Harram, so upon him is the expiation’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub, from ibn Ri’ab from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “

I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who finds a bird in non-al-Haram (the sacred area) and buys it, then enters al-Haram (the sacred area), with it and it dies. He (the Imam) said, ‘Were he to release it in al-Haram (the sacred area), then it died he did not owe anything. If he holds it until it dies with him in al-Haram (the sacred area) he is required to pay ransom.’”
